svg.title: Retrieval without embeddings. BM25F lite drives ranking, with field weights folded into term frequencies: title 3, questions 3, keywords 2, fund names 2, text 1, and adjacent word bigrams indexed alongside single words. TF IDF cosine multiplied by IDF coverage produces the confidence score. Cosine alone was fooled: 'what is the capital of Mongolia' matched the capital gains document at 0.29. Coverage asks what share of the question's IDF mass the document accounts for and charges unseen words at maximum IDF, pushing such questions below the floor. The answer floor is 0.06, chosen because the hardest off topic question peaks at 0.052. A fund affinity pass boosts the scheme named in the question, so the midcap exit load cannot be answered with the large cap figure. Embeddings were skipped because sentence transformers pulls in about 2 GB of torch, which does not fit a free serverless tier.

div.h2: Retrieval that knows when it does not know

div.p: Weights fold into term frequencies before scoring. Bigrams are indexed next to single words. Fund affinity boosts the scheme the question names and suppresses the other three, so a midcap question never gets the large cap figure.
Why no embeddings? sentence transformers pulls in about 2 GB of torch. That does not fit a free serverless tier, and cold starts would take tens of seconds.

div.div: Confidence = TF IDF cosine × IDF coverage

"What is the capital of Mongolia" matched the capital gains document at 0.29 on cosine alone. Coverage asks how much of the question's IDF mass a document explains, and charges unseen words like Mongolia at maximum IDF. That pushes them under the floor.
div.p: 0.06 was picked from a sweep: it answers 97.6% of real questions with zero false answers.
